steps.text: Combine carrots and brown sugar in a medium bowl. Let sit for 1 hour, then stir in raisins.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour two 10-inch round cake pans. Beat eggs in a large bowl until light in color.
Gradually beat in white sugar, oil, and vanilla. Stir in pineapple.
Combine flour, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl, then stir into egg mixture until absorbed.
Stir in carrot mixture and walnuts. Pour evenly into the prepared cake pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes before removing cake from the pans; let cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Carrot Cake Ever
raw_recipe.description: The best carrot cake recipe uses grated carrots, crushed pineapple, and juicy raisins to create the most deliciously moist and tender cake ever!

review.reviewBody: Before I decided to try this cake I read every single review, paying careful attention to those who did not like the cake very much. Though the overwhelming majority, of which I am now a part, liked this cake very much I understand that you learn a lot more about something by learning what people did not like about it. So, after having made the cake I have a few suggestions for those who didn’t like the cake. Most of the complaints where that the cake was too heavy or that it was too moist or “pudding like” A solution to this might be to strain the carrots and pineapple more before adding them in to the cake batter. I know the recipe doesn’t specify but I strained the carrots and the pineapple until they where almost dry and added about 2 – 3 tablespoons of the strained liquid back in. I also hydrated the raisins a bit by letting them sit in a cup of warm water while the carrots sat in the brown sugar. Also I made 3 - 8” rounds instead of the recommended 2 - 10” rounds. This will shorten the bake time to about 30 -45 mins. and may also help solve any underdone cake problems… I thought this cake was very good and well worth the effort. Everyone I have served this to has loved this and I certainly plan on making it again.

This carrot cake is the absolute best that I have ever made. I had many compliments on this. The cake is large and serves many. It only took 40 minutes to bake. I used my own cream cheese frosting recipe which I think is much better and has a richer flavor. It is as follows 1/4 lb. soft butter, 8 oz. cream cheese, 1 tsp vanilla and 1 lb. confectioners sugar.
Combine butter, cream cheese and vanilla, mix till blended. Add sugar and mix til smooth. Enjoy I do not think you will be dissappointed.

I got rave reviews on this cake ("you should sell this for $8.00 a slice"), but I did mess with the recipe. 
First, I scaled the recipe to 12 servings because of the comments about how huge the cake was. I used 2 9" baking pans and it made a pretty regular sized cake. 
I used about 4 cups grated carrots, which was all of the carrots in the bag I bought and 1/2 cup less than called for. I replaced half of the oil with apple sauce and I replaced half of the pineapple with apple sauce. I also used wheat flour for a little less than 1/2 of the flour. I left out the raisins and I added about a tsp each of nutmeg, allspice, ginger and dried orange rind. I also doubled the cinnamon. 
For the frosting I used 1/4 lb butter, 8 oz cream cheese, 2 tsp vanilla and 1 lb sifted conf sugar. Should probably have refrigerated it to let it set more before I transported it because it got a little slippy but not disastrous.
I took it to a 4 person dinner party and brought leftovers to work. People could not get enough. I was pretty happy since I not only never made carrot cake before, I had never eaten it so I wasn't sure how it should taste! Thanks!
It was great! I baked it in a 9 x 13 cake pan at 375 degrees for 45 minutes.

My wedding cake was a carrot cake and each anniversary for the last 17 years, I have been making carrot cake recipes. Through the years, I have tried many recipes but none of them were "THE" recipe - until now!! With the exception of baking the cake in 3 9" pans, I didn't change a thing and the cake was definitely "bakery" quality. The cake is also a very pretty color. A food processor definitely takes the burden out of the grating! I also used 1 1/2 recipes of the cream cheese II frosting recipe and that appeared to be a sufficient amount of frosting.

This recipe is - as it stands - the best carrot cake ever. It has replaced a local (and very good) baker where we used to buy our carrot cake (I now make it for my family). I've baked this at least 5-7 times over the past year (every time after the first time was upon request of my family). I don't think the recipe needs to be modified at all, it's moist, flavorful, and has so much substance as is. I use a food processor to grate the carrots, so prep time for me isn't that lengthy (I wouldn't want to grate those carrots manually). Also, I use the baby carrots that are already peeled and pre-packaged, simply for ease of prep...no adverse impact on the cake. One note: I tried one time using whole wheat flour (I wanted to see if I could get same great taste with a bit of a healthier flare) and it didn't work out...the whole wheat sacrificed some of the moisture, and the cake ended up being a bit too dry.

Delicious! I made 3 8” pans and cooked for 35min approx. I marinated the carrots in the sugar for over an hour and drained them really well, added 6 Tablespoons of the liquid to the batter, drained the pineapple really well and also soaked the raisins for 10-20min in boiling water. Super moist and delicious loved by all will definitely make this again & again .

Followed many of the suggestions of CrystalLaurey (6/1/2004 review) - drained the pinapple well and removed most of liquid from the carrot/sugar mixture. Added back 3 tablespoons of this liquid to the batter. Used 9 inch rounds and did NOT put every last bit of batter in them (made a small side cake in a mini loaf pan). Only needed 35 minutes to bake the 9 inch rounds at 350 deg. What a great cake! Used a simple icing with 4 cups powdered sugar, 8 oz cream cheese, 1/2 cup butter and 1 tsp vanilla. So happy with the results!

This was a great recipe. 👍🏻I squeezed the pineapple dry. And drained all but two tablespoons of liquid from the carrots. Fresh grated nutmeg if you have it, is a must!Made this butter cream cheese frosting and Voila!!1 brick cream cheese very soft1/2 cup salted butter very soft1 tsp vanilla3 cups sifted icing sugar. (Or to your desired sweetness is achieved.Mix cream cheese and butter on med high, add vanilla then mix until nice and combined. Gradually add in powdered sugar.

This has been my go-to carrot cake recipe for many years! I've served it to countless people who claim to 'hate' carrot cake and love this version. After reading many of the reviews - and coming from someone who has mastered this recipe - I'd like to add my 2 cents: #1 - add the raisins to the carrots/brown sugar mixture to hydrate them AND save the extra step of doing it separately, #2 - I do not strain the carrots because it's the liquid that gives this cake it's moistness (and there is nothing worse than a dry carrot cake), although I do strain the pineapple, #3 - I prefer 3x8" cake pans because it does make a taller cake and definitely a more impressive presentation for those special occasions, #4 - use a cream cheese icing as it enhances the flavor of the carrot cake but make sure it's a good quality recipe because some cream cheese icings can be too sweet and too thin in consistency. You need a good, solid icing, and #5 - use dowels or straws to support the weight of this cake, especially if you're doing 3 layers and will be transporting it. As an aside, I baked this cake for a former boss years ago for his birthday because carrot cake was his favorite and a co-worker who hated carrot cake ended up loving it. Loved it so much that a few years later, she requested one for her family's Christmas celebrations....she said everyone loved it and that she still hates carrot cake, except for mine!

I made this for a friend who does not cook but has a crazy love for carrot cake. He frequently orders carrot cake at several different restaurants in the area as well as his favorite bakery. He said this recipe beats all of them! I was leery of using all the "juice" from the carrots and brown sugar, but it worked fine. I decreased the white sugar by 1/2 cup and used a regular bundt pan and all the batter fit perfectly. For personal preference I added a couple teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice along with 2 teaspoons of regular cinnamon. I baked it at 350 as instructed in my air fryer/oven and it needed an extra 10-12 minutes for the toothpick to come out clean. I used the basic cream cheese frosting and added chopped walnuts. It is a dense cake but so divine!
Good recipe!
Its dense, sweet, and delicious. I soaked my raisins in rum before adding it to the batter, yum!

This is my go too, I usually use cake pans with lids from grocery store I travel with it, It’s perfect the way it is. I totally agree with squeezing the liquid out. It’s meant to be a dense cake. Love it.
LOVE this cake Easy to follow. My raisins were dried and no Sultans ( my preferred raisins) so I substituted dried cranberries. Great looking colour effect!

This was my first time baking a carrot cake, at my Dad’s request for his birthday. However, I am the only gluten-free person in our family and I’d like to have some cake too!! Alterations to recipe - I used King Arthur’s 1 for 1 flour, I forgot to buy applesauce so I used 3/4 cup buttermilk for moisture, and I had pecans instead of walnuts. It was phenomenal. No one had any idea it was gf, and absolutely loved it. Definitely a keeper.

Excellent recipe - we bought pre-shredded carrots and that sped things up a lot. I wish the icing recipe was built into this one, I didn't notice it at first and cost me a second trip to the store. The step where you let the brown sugar and carrots sit for an hour... wow, neat to see osmosis in action! So much liquid comes out of the carrots! Follow the directions carefully and slowly and this comes out to be an AMAZING cake. We left out the walnuts for an allergy, and everyone loved this cake.
Made it once before it was successful they ate every crumb...
Best ever! Have been making this for years. Love it, so moist.

I'm thrilled with this carrot cake recipe! Best I've tried to make and I think the best I've ever eaten! Moist and flavorful. Made it for my husband's birthday, and everyone absolutely loved it! Made three 9-inch layers, baked around 33 min. Used a cream cheese frosting recipe I already had.
